maria.devex: Heads-up — hitting a weird failure when using the Python client against Dedicated with a corporate proxy + custom truststore. Request just hangs sometimes and other times throws CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
ryan.eng-runtime: ugh. Can you paste a short repro? is this sync or async?
alex.devex: Also: does this only happen when base_url is set to the dedicated endpoint or with any non-default base_url?
maria.devex: Repro (async):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], base_url="https://dedicated.customer.region.redwood.internal", verify="/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem")
# using aio client under the hood, default timeout
await client.chat.create(...)
```
Behavior: when HTTP(S)_PROXY is set in environment, client sometimes hangs on connect for ~30s, then raises "ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed". If I unset HTTP(S)_PROXY it succeeds.
ryan.eng-runtime: hmm. Our aiohttp session by default uses trust_env=False in some layers, which bypasses env proxy settings — but hangs+ssl error sounds like mix of proxy negotiation + incorrect CA being used. Are you also setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE?
maria.devex: We set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE in CI, but the issue reproduces locally even when passing verify path to the client.
sophia.eng-ml: Could be we create an SSLContext incorrectly for async path — if verify is a path we should call ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...) and pass that into aiohttp, otherwise aiohttp expects boolean or ssl.SSLContext.
alex.devex: I ran a quick experiment: when I set env NO_PROXY for the dedicated host the call succeeds immediately. So proxy is definitely involved.
ryan.eng-runtime: Thanks — two actionable leads: 1) our client should accept a path for verify on both sync and async and translate it to SSLContext consistently; 2) ensure aiohttp honors trust_env or reads proxy env when trust_env True.
maria.devex: Agree on (1). For (2) I think current codebase forces trust_env=False in the internal transport to avoid leaking corporate proxies in hosted mode, but for Dedicated/Private we must allow proxy/VPC behavior. Maybe tie trust_env to whether base_url is in internal network or a dedicated config flag.
ryan.eng-runtime: Good point. We can add config flag `trust_env_proxies: bool` and default to False for hosted, True for dedicated/private. Need to ensure it's documented and tests added.
maria.devex: Agree on (1). For acceptance criteria: - passing verify="/path/to/ca.pem" works for async and sync - env proxies respected when trust_env_proxies=True - clear log message: "proxy handshake failed" vs "certificate verification failed" - unit test simulating proxy env and custom CA
ryan.eng-runtime: I'll open an RFC/PR. Tentative plan: create helper that normalizes `verify` into either bool or SSLContext, and a transport factory that accepts trust_env_proxies flag. I'll add a small integration test using a local mitmproxy in CI to validate behavior.
sophia.eng-ml: FYI, we should also call this out in Dedicated onboarding doc so customers know to set NO_PROXY for the private control plane if they want to bypass corp proxies.
maria.devex: +1. Also encountered a subtle one: when verify points to a directory of certs instead of a single file, behavior differs between sync/async. Let's make the API accept both cafile and capath and normalize.
ryan.eng-runtime: noted. I'll draft the PR with tests. tagging @deploy-bot to run CI when ready.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline queued for branch rryan/proxy-ssl-fix — build #4321. :rocket:
alex.devex: Thanks! assigning to ryan to shepherd. If anyone can help with a minimal repro container (mitmproxy + custom CA) I can run the integration locally.
maria.devex: I can put together a tiny docker-compose with mitmproxy tonight. Will share gist. :thumbsup:
ryan.eng-runtime: awesome — appreciate it. I'll follow up with an issue number and link to PR in this thread.
